# Neo — Design System

> Material UI theme (v5 and v6) + semantic tokens + icons + components.
> Figma is the source of truth: when in visual doubt, the master rules.

Each component has its spec (`docs/components/<x>.md`): when it is used and when not, its anatomy with
the master's measurements, its states, its accessibility and its API. The types the package publishes
(`.d.ts`) are its exact signature.

## Components

- [Alert](docs/components/alert.md): Communicates system messages the user needs to read. Axes: type. React: `import { NeoAlert } from '@neo-design/mui'`.
- [AnnouncementBar](docs/components/announcement-bar.md): Gives an operational notice —hours, care, services— above everything, over the header. It is not a semantic message: it informs about how the institution works today. React: `import { NeoAnnouncementBar } from '@neo-design/mui'`.
- [AspectRatio](docs/components/aspect-ratio.md): Fixes the proportion (width: height) of the content and keeps it when the size changes. Axes: ratio. React: `import { NeoAspectRatio } from '@neo-design/mui'`.
- [Badge](docs/components/badge.md): Communicates system state or an activity count, compactly. Axes: type. React: `import { NeoBadge } from '@neo-design/mui'`.
- [Banner](docs/components/banner.md): Highlights a message within the page —a campaign, a benefit, a notice— with or without an action. Axes: size, full-photo (prop `fullPhoto`). React: `import { NeoBanner } from '@neo-design/mui'`.
- [BottomSheet](docs/components/bottom-sheet.md): Rises from the bottom edge on mobile with complementary content that can wait, or a short task, while the person can still see and return to the page underneath. React: `import { NeoBottomSheet } from '@neo-design/mui'`.
- [BrandLoader](docs/components/brand-loader.md): Accompanies the wait for a relevant action of the person and says what is being resolved. It is used as a full-screen transition view, between the action and its result. React: `import { NeoBrandLoader } from '@neo-design/mui'`.
- [Button](docs/components/button.md): Runs actions. Axes: type (prop `family`), size, variant, surface. React: `import { NeoButton } from '@neo-design/mui'`.
- [ButtonIcon](docs/components/button-icon.md): Runs an action that is understood by its icon: close, back, add, more options. Axes: type (prop `family`), size, variant, surface. React: `import { NeoButtonIcon } from '@neo-design/mui'`.
- [Checkbox](docs/components/checkbox.md): Multiple, independent selection. React: `import { NeoCheckbox } from '@neo-design/mui'`.
- [Chips](docs/components/chips.md): Compact interactive filter or selection within the same view. React: `import { NeoChips } from '@neo-design/mui'`.
- [ChipsGroup](docs/components/chips-group.md): A row of related chips chosen together: several at once, or one at a time. React: `import { NeoChipsGroup } from '@neo-design/mui'`.
- [Combobox](docs/components/combobox.md): Single selection from a list filterable by text: you type and the list narrows down to the matches. React: `import { NeoCombobox } from '@neo-design/mui'`.
- [Drawer](docs/components/drawer.md): Enters from the right edge on the web with complementary or extensive content that the person opens on demand, while the page underneath stays in view. React: `import { NeoDrawer } from '@neo-design/mui'`.
- [EmptyState](docs/components/empty-state.md): Takes the place of content that does not exist yet and says what can be done about it. React: `import { NeoEmptyState } from '@neo-design/mui'`.
- [Link](docs/components/link.md): Takes the person somewhere else. React: `import { NeoLink } from '@neo-design/mui'`.
- [Menu](docs/components/menu.md): Public floating-list primitive: the reusable panel of options. React: `import { NeoMenu } from '@neo-design/mui'`.
- [ModalDialog](docs/components/modal-dialog.md): Interrupts the flow to ask for a decision or an answer. Axes: type, size. React: `import { NeoModalDialog } from '@neo-design/mui'`.
- [ModalFullscreen](docs/components/modal-fullscreen.md): Takes over the whole screen for dense information or a long task, without losing the point of origin. React: `import { NeoModalFullscreen } from '@neo-design/mui'`.
- [RadioButton](docs/components/radio-button.md): Exclusive selection among mutually exclusive options. Axes: direction. React: `import { NeoRadioButton } from '@neo-design/mui'`.
- [Select](docs/components/select.md): Single selection of one option from a predefined set. React: `import { NeoSelect } from '@neo-design/mui'`.
- [Skeleton](docs/components/skeleton.md): A loading placeholder with the shape of the content to come. It goes on the first load of a page or a section whose structure is already known — lists, tables, cards, profiles — and only where the content comes from the service: the content takes its place all at once. Axes: variant. React: `import { NeoSkeleton } from '@neo-design/mui'`.
- [Snackbar](docs/components/snackbar.md): Communicates, for a moment, the result of an action or a change in the system, without interrupting the task. It floats over the page and goes away on its own. React: `import { NeoSnackbar } from '@neo-design/mui'`.
- [Spinner](docs/components/spinner.md): Indicator for a brief, localized load. Axes: size. React: `import { NeoSpinner } from '@neo-design/mui'`.
- [Tabs](docs/components/tabs.md): Organizes content into sections within a single view. React: `import { NeoTabs } from '@neo-design/mui'`.
- [Tag](docs/components/tag.md): Informational classification label: which category an element belongs to. Axes: tone. React: `import { NeoTag } from '@neo-design/mui'`.
- [TextField](docs/components/text-field.md): Text input typed by the person. Axes: type. React: `import { NeoTextField } from '@neo-design/mui'`.
- [Toggle](docs/components/toggle.md): On/off control with immediate effect. React: `import { NeoToggle } from '@neo-design/mui'`.
- [Tooltip](docs/components/tooltip.md): Contextual informational label about the element that triggers it. Axes: placement. React: `import { NeoTooltip } from '@neo-design/mui'`.
- [TextArea](docs/components/text-field.md): realizes `text-field` together with `NeoTextField`, and one spec covers both. React: `import { NeoTextArea } from '@neo-design/mui'`.
- [RadioGroup](docs/components/radio-button.md): realizes `radio-button` together with `NeoRadioButton`, and one spec covers both. React: `import { NeoRadioGroup } from '@neo-design/mui'`.

## Tokens

- [packages/foundations/tokens/neo-color.css](packages/foundations/tokens/neo-color.css): 94 semantic color tokens. They are consumed by role —fill, text, border or icon, plus an intent—, never by value.
- [packages/foundations/tokens/neo-foundations.css](packages/foundations/tokens/neo-foundations.css): 239 dimensional tokens — spacing, radii, strokes, typography.
- [docs/MODEL.md](docs/MODEL.md): the grammar of a token name, on one page.
- **Semantic tokens resolve to a direct value, with no `var()` chains — and that is a decision, not a gap**:
  primitives do not ship (if a color is missing, a ROLE is missing), and two roles that share a hex are
  independent on purpose — chaining them would invent a relationship the design does not have.

## How to consume it in a React app

Order matters — the first external eval showed an agent vendoring the CSS layer because it did not
find this paragraph:

1. **Mount the theme, once**: `import { theme } from '@neo-design/mui'` (the alias
`@neo-design/mui/theme` also exists) + `<ThemeProvider theme={theme}><CssBaseline/>` —`CssBaseline` is required:
   it brings the CSS variables—, the font (`@fontsource/noto-sans`, weights 400, 500 and 700) and the icon sprite
   injected once (`import { sprite } from '@neo-design/foundations/sprite'`, in a hidden element). With that, the `@mui/material` components
   (`Button`, `Alert`, `Dialog`, `Chip`…) come out with Neo styling — the system's 25, not
   only the ones that have a wrapper. **With 4 exceptions, and they are structural, not cosmetic:**
`TextField` → use `NeoTextField`, `TextField multiline` → use `NeoTextArea`, `Select` → use `NeoSelect`, `Autocomplete` → use `NeoCombobox`. In those, MUI puts the label inside the
   border and the master wants it above the field: a theme changes style, not structure. Details and
   checklist: docs/dev/INTEGRATION.md.
2. **The `Neo*` wrappers** add the system's API where MUI falls short:
`import { NeoButton } from '@neo-design/mui'` — the package's single entry point, with no internal
   paths. Each component's row (above) says which one has a wrapper and which one is used as themed
   MUI.
3. **The plain CSS layer** (`packages/foundations/css/`) implements each component without depending on MUI: it is
   for surfaces WITHOUT React. In a React app it is not copied or vendored — the theme already brings
   everything.

## Figma — the source of truth

The repo MIRRORS these files; never the other way around. When code and Figma disagree, the master is measured.
(Section generated from the ecosystem registry — the single home of these keys.)

- **tokens** · `ml3ScFhJNwgs6xZpKUKuok` — Semantics + Layout + Primitives — the source of truth for values
- **icons** · `zIbuWAvLhwTlwnVwbDgY5n` — the icons, in three families
- **ds** · `9FoTERLTyDXz3gmPLjjJ09` — the component masters — they consume Tokens and Icons
- **workflow** · `VrZLhxdMqBeK3JrSP3v4kF` — the process scaffolding: notes, QA, mockup chrome
- **ilustraciones** · `q1m7Dkvtje8v7ZTzX6uc8E` — OPS-Library-Ilustraciones: illustrations with their own tokens

## Rules an agent must follow

- One visually dominant action per view.
- Colors come from the semantic tokens; a hand-written hex is an error.
- A field's label is visible and static. Help text and the error message share ONE slot: in `error`, that slot says the error.
- States the browser already provides (hover, focus) are never props.
- **`onChange` receives the event first, as in MUI — the value is never the first argument.** `(event, checked)`: `NeoCheckbox`, `NeoRadioButton`, `NeoToggle`. `(event, value)`: `NeoChipsGroup`, `NeoRadioGroup`, `NeoTabs`. `(event, value, reason)` (the signature of MUI `Autocomplete`): `NeoCombobox`. `(event)` (the value is `event.target.value`): `NeoTextArea`, `NeoTextField`.
- **A component accepts more props than the system decided.** The wrappers pass what they do not
  recognize to the base MUI component, so `<NeoButton fullWidth>` *works* even though the system
  has no full-width button: the master does not have it and the system does not declare it. That is
  not a shortcut, it is leaving the system without anything warning you. The only thing used freely is
`sx` for **the consumer's layout** —margins, gap, position— because layout is a separate layer and
  does not reach the system; for appearance, never: the theme decides that.
- **When Neo lacks a component** (table, sidebar, progress bar, avatar, selectable card, navigation item with an active state), the answer depends on where the need
  comes from. If no design delivered it: the Material UI component with the theme mounted, not restyled by hand.
  If a design delivered it and the library does not have it yet: build it with the semantic tokens its design
  names, never with a hex value or a primitive. Details: docs/dev/SUPPORT.md.

## Building a screen

- **Color is mostly neutral: 80 / 20 / 10.** About 80 % is neutral: the page, panels and cards sit on `surface/base/default` and `surface/base/secondary`. About 20 % is the dark navy, mostly as text, with `surface/base/inverse` kept to a few pieces. About 10 % is the coral brand color, as the accent in the details: brand icons, icon containers, the brand action. Never a large dark or coral panel competing with another strong color.
- **A link is always underlined and takes the color of the text around it.** In navigation and footers too: there is no link without underline. Do not color it: on a dark footer the surrounding text is already light, and the link inherits it.
- **A link that stands alone takes its size and weight from `variant`**: `bodyMdBold` at 14 px, `bodyLgBold` at 16, `titleSmBold` at 18, `captionSmMedium` at 12. Bold, because a link is not told apart by color. Inside a sentence it takes nothing and inherits the paragraph. Do not hang a class with `font-*` on a link: in the usual stylesheet order the theme wins and the class does nothing.
- **Titles take their size and weight from a type style** (`display-*`, `headline-*`, `title-*`). A hand-written `font-size` or `font-weight` is an error, like a hand-written hex: if no style fits, the hierarchy is missing a level, not a size.
- **The info icon that opens help is `semantic-info`, filled** (`semantic-info-inverse` on a dark background), never the outlined `system` one and never recolored: the color and the fill say it can be pressed and opens help.

## Implementing a Figma node

- **When the node does not say it, ask: do not invent it.** The options of a select, what an action does, the error and empty texts: if neither the node nor the brief gives them, write the question down (in `QUESTIONS.md` or in your answer) and leave a visible placeholder. Invented content looks finished and nobody reviews it.
- **Reuse what the project already built.** Before writing a layout piece —a section, a row of actions, a card— look at the screens next to it: if one already exports it, import it. Two copies of the same layout drift apart.
- **From a Figma node to code: one instance, one `Neo*`.** Each instance of a Neo Design System master becomes its `Neo*` component with the properties the instance sets; when the node carries a Code Connect snippet, that snippet is the code: copy it as is. A `…` in the snippet marks what design cannot say —the destination of a link, the handler of an action—: complete it from the task or ask; never leave it empty nor invent it. A property left at its default is not written. Frames become layout with the `--neo-space-*` tokens; sizes and colors of the node are never copied by hand.

## Accessibility that belongs to the screen

Each Neo component is accessible on its own. The screen that combines them still owns these:

- **Focus follows reading order.** Put the components in the DOM in the order they are read. Never fix
  the order with a positive `tabindex` or by reordering with CSS: sighted and keyboard users get two
  different screens.
- **One `h1` per view, and no skipped heading levels.** A component's title is part of that outline. With
  an image, `NeoBottomSheet` has no title slot: give your content a heading and point `aria-labelledby` at it.
- **Landmarks.** One `main`, plus `header`, `nav` and `footer` where the screen has them. A second
`nav` needs its own `aria-label`.
- **Every route has its own `<title>`**, so whoever arrives knows where they are.
- **On a client-side route change, move focus** to the new view's `h1` or to `main`. Otherwise focus stays
  on a link that is no longer there.
- **A live region has to exist before its message.** Text injected into a region that was just created is
  often not announced: render the empty region first, then change its text.
- **Do not manage focus around the overlays.** `NeoModalDialog`, `NeoModalFullscreen`, `NeoBottomSheet` and `NeoDrawer`
  move focus in when they open, keep it inside, and return it to what opened them when they close.
